Presented side by side without the rule, 12.5% reads as higher than Sudan's 2.9%, which is the cross-rule artefact. The comparison the scorecard relies on (Karabakh lower than Sudan) holds only under a common rule.
raw.evidence: data/derived/results/h7_scored.json: primary karabakh rule 5km_2d observed 0.125 (n=40); sudan rule 1km_12h observed 0.0294 (n=680); secondary karabakh 1km_12h 0.0, sudan 5km_2d 0.176; karabakh_lower_than_sudan_primary_cross_rule false; note says the 1 km row is the like-for-like comparison.
raw.fix: Add 'under different matching rules (Karabakh 5 km / 2 days, Sudan 1 km / 12 h); on a common rule Karabakh is lower than Sudan' after the two figures.

raw.problem: Could not trace the 3.8% (V-test placebo) to a results file outside the ACLED-named files. The only non-ACLED hits for 'placebo' are the robustness files and Telegram (0.65%), which carry different numbers. DEVIATIONS says the placebo script is 21_acled_grade.py, which is in the out-of-scope area. 'Most' is also a stretch: 3.8 of 5.0 is 76% of the match rate.

raw.paper_says: Fires do not lead Russian gains at a size that matters: with raw fires the test is inconclusive, and after correcting for what the sensor could see, the 90% interval sits inside the smallest effect we pre-registered as meaningful (equivalence).
raw.problem: This reads a null as proof of absence. Under PREREG H6, 'inconclusive' means a meaningful effect cannot be ruled out: the raw-fire 90% CI goes up to 1.82 under CRV1 and 2.04 under Driscoll–Kraay, both above the SESOI of 1.70. The paper's own confirmatory tables also show fire terms that are significant and at or above a meaningful size: H9 has lead 8 at β 0.98, significant under both methods and above the 1-week SESOI of 0.65; H10 has small fires on the Ukrainian-held side at β 4.41, p<0.001 under both; H11 phase B is β 0.87, significant under both. The abstract's blanket 'do not lead' contradicts §5.3–5.5.
raw.evidence: data/derived/results/h6_lead.json H6.lf ci90_crv1 [0.13,1.82], ci90_dk [-0.09,2.04], sesoi 1.703; verdicts.json H9 'peak lead 8 (β 0.982, p_wild 0.000, p_dk 0.002)', 1-week SESOI 0.65; H10 'small_ua_side β 4.412 (p_wild 0.000, p_dk 0.000)'; H11 'β_B 0.873 (p_wild 0.001, p_dk 0.018)'
raw.fix: Abstract: "We found no evidence that fires lead Russian gains at a size that matters, but could not rule one out with raw fires (inconclusive); with the corrected index the effect is inside the pre-registered smallest meaningful size (equivalence). The pre-registered secondary tests found some fire terms that were significant but not predicted (an 8-week lead; small fires on the Ukrainian-held side), which we do not interpret."

raw.paper_says: Once you account for when the sensor could see, the small raw association between fires and next month's Russian gains shrinks toward zero, which suggests some of the raw signal was the sensor's visibility, not the war.
raw.problem: The corrected index divides fires by a modelled P(detect) that is clipped at 0.02 for 49.8% of cell-weeks (mean 0.036). So log1p(fires/p) mostly adds about 3.9 log-units to any non-zero week and leaves zero weeks at 0. That changes the regressor's scale and shape, which alone can shrink β per log-unit. Opportunity is already a control in H6, so the step from 'β shrinks' to 'the signal was visibility' is not identified. The P(detect) model also failed its own criterion (AUC 0.737), and it was trained on whether filmed events got a match, which is not the same as the chance that a given fire is detected. The clip is in the figure caption and the planning note but not in Methods or DEVIATIONS.
raw.evidence: h6_lead.json p_detect {mean 0.036, median 0.0201, share_clipped_at_0.02 0.498, clip 0.02}; planning/PANEL.md line 68 'clip P at 0.02 and state it'; §3 says only 'raw fires divided by the modelled probability of detection'
raw.fix: §3: add "P(detect) is clipped at 0.02; 50% of front cell-weeks sit at the clip." §5.2: replace "which suggests some of the raw signal was the sensor's visibility, not the war" with "Because the corrected regressor has a different scale (half of cell-weeks sit at the 0.02 clip), the change in category does not show by itself that the raw association came from visibility." Log the clip in DEVIATIONS under operational definitions.

raw.paper_says: FIRMS matched **1.26%** within 1 km / ±12 h, against a placebo of 0.65%
raw.problem: The window is described wrongly. In the code, the Telegram match uses [event_ts − 1 h, event_ts + 12 h] for timestamped events (13,949 of 18,404), and for date-only events the Kyiv date −1 h to +12 h. It is not the 48-hour ±12 h window of H1. The placebo is one-sided (7 days earlier only), not ±7 days like the V placebo. So 1.26% is not comparable with H1's 5.0% or the V placebo, and the text invites that comparison.
raw.evidence: scripts/telegram/50_aggregate.py lines 15–18 ('[event_ts - 1 h, event_ts + 12 h] (date-only events: the whole Kyiv date - 1 h .. + 12 h ...) plus a placebo column for the same place and window 7 days earlier'); firms_match_cellweek_meta.json by_window_kind ts n 13,949 match 0.0062, date n 4,455 match 0.0323
raw.fix: "FIRMS matched 1.26% within 1 km in a 13-hour window from 1 h before to 12 h after the reported time (date-only reports: the local day), against 0.65% for the same place and window 7 days earlier. The window is narrower than H1's 48 hours, so the rate is not comparable with H1."

raw.paper_says: The sensor almost never sees them.
raw.problem: A 1 km test cannot support 'almost never sees' when the points are place centroids. 3,320 strikes are geocoded only to a raion (district) and 663 to a hromada seat (municipal centre), and the rest to settlement centroids. The pipeline's own comment says settlement centroids sit kilometres from the actual hit in towns. DEVIATIONS 2026-10-27 uses exactly this argument to reject a 1 km rule for coarsely placed UCDP events ('would measure geocoding error, not the sensor'). At the 3 km diagnostic radius the match is 5.5% against a 4.0% placebo. The extraction hand-check scored whether the place name was right, not whether the point lies within 1 km of the hit.
raw.evidence: firms_match_cellweek_meta.json by_geo_level: raion n 3,320 match 0.0003, hromada_seat n 663, settlement n 14,413 match 0.0159; overall match_3km 0.0546, placebo_3km 0.0397; 50_aggregate.py line 54 comment 'settlement centroids sit km from the actual hit in towns'; DEVIATIONS 2026-10-27 'A 1 km rule on events placed only to within 25 km or a province would measure geocoding error, not the sensor.'
raw.fix: Replace with: "Most reports are geocoded to a settlement or district centre, often kilometres from the impact, so a 1 km match mixes sensor misses with geocoding error; 3,983 strikes placed only at district or municipal level cannot be matched at 1 km at all. At 3 km the match is 5.5% against a 4.0% placebo."

raw.paper_says: two paid research assistants hand-checked a stratified sample of 200 extracted strikes
raw.problem: This overstates the coverage. Of the 200-row sample, 35 agree rows were never seen by a person. One rater (PD) checked 165 impact rows. The other rater (AT) checked only the 20 shared impact rows, plus 35 empty-list posts and 100 typing rows. So 165 rows were checked, by one person each except for 20.
raw.evidence: planning/QA_HANDCHECK.md lines 78–79 '135 iffy rows (all checked) and 65 agree rows (30 audited, 35 never seen by a person)'; line 59 AT ingested 'imp-001..020'; REPORT.md checked counts 30 + 135
raw.fix: "Two paid research assistants checked a stratified sample of extracted strikes: one checked 165 of 200 sampled rows, both checked the same 20 to measure agreement, and 35 rows the triage had machine-cleared have not been checked by anyone yet."

raw.paper_says: Weighted to the sample, the model had the place right in **92%** of strikes, the weapon in 94% ..., the target type in 97% and the casualty count in 91%; all clear the 85% threshold set in advance.
raw.problem: These are presented as final scores that passed a test set in advance. The decision rule fixed in advance says that once the 30-row audit finds any error in a field, the raters check that field on every agree row and the accuracy is recomputed on the full set. The audit found errors in place, target type, casualties and date, and the 35-row check has not been done. So under the paper's own rule, those four figures are provisional estimates scaled up from 30 audited rows to 65. DEVIATIONS 2026-11-09 promises they are 'labelled as such'; 'Weighted to the sample' is not that label. The caveat ('Thirty-five machine-cleared rows...') comes four sentences later and does not connect to these numbers. Casualties had 3 errors in 30 audited rows, so the unchecked rows could plausibly pull it close to 85%.
raw.evidence: planning/QA_HANDCHECK.md line 32–34 decision rule; REPORT.md 'agree label trusted' False for place, target_type, casualties, time; DEVIATIONS 2026-11-09 item 3 'the reported accuracies weight the 30 audited rows up to the 65-row bucket instead, and are labelled as such'
raw.fix: "Provisional, pending a human check of 35 machine-cleared rows that the pre-set rule requires (the audit found errors in four of five fields), the extraction had the place right in about 92% of strikes, the target type in 97%, the casualty count in 91% and the weapon in 90–94%. These estimates clear the 85% bar set in advance, but the check that decides it is not finished."

raw.paper_says: The date was right in 98%, scored from the one rater whose instructions matched the extraction rule (90% if the other rater's answers on 20 shared rows are counted; that choice was made after seeing the answers).
raw.problem: The 98% is not a human check of the date. The packet never showed raters the post's publication date, which is where the model's date comes from. After the first rater returned, the second rater was told to 'answer Yes unless the post states a different date or time'. A default-yes instruction given after seeing results, then scored from that rater only, makes the headline the least conservative figure available. The disclosure is there, but the post-hoc number leads and the conservative one sits in parentheses.
raw.evidence: planning/QA_HANDCHECK.md lines 61–63 ('the packet never shows the post's publication date ... Not scoreable by humans as asked ... tell PD to answer Yes unless the post states a different date or time'); line 87 date/time combined 90.2%, PD alone 98.4%, agreement 6/20; DEVIATIONS 2026-11-09 item 1
raw.fix: "Raters could not verify the date as asked (the packet did not show the post date), so date accuracy is not human-checked: the two-rater score is 90%; one rater, told after the first returns to answer yes unless the post gave a different date, scored 98%."

raw.paper_says: Posts where the model extracted nothing were mostly daily statistics lists, which the extraction prompt skips by design.
raw.problem: The paper leaves out the measured number: raters judged 62.9% (95% CI 46–77%, n=35) of posts with no extracted strike to contain a strike. The 'mostly statistics lists, about 0–2 true misses' reading comes from the author's own review of one rater's 35 answers. It was not adjudicated by a second person, and DEVIATIONS lists this as one of the three questions where the guide wording did not match the extraction rules. The 76% post-type accuracy is also not reported.
raw.evidence: data/derived/telegram/qa/REPORT.md 'empty | missed_post_rate | 62.9% | 46.3%–76.8% | 35'; 'typing | post_type | 76.0%'; planning/QA_HANDCHECK.md lines 64–67 (one rater, author's reading, 'about 0-2')
raw.fix: "Raters marked 63% (22 of 35) of posts with no extracted strike as containing one; on our reading most of these are daily statistics lists that the extraction skips by design, but that reading has not been adjudicated. Post-type labels were right in 76% of 100 posts."

raw.paper_says: FIRMS caught 5.0% of held-out confirmed events. Under clear night skies in summer it caught 7.4%. ... The point is the gradient. In a Ukrainian winter the sensor is effectively off.
raw.problem: 'Caught' describes detection, but the same abstract says most matches are background fire (placebo 3.8% against 5.0%), and §4.8 says the best stratum beats chance by only about 1.4–1.5×. So about two thirds of the best-stratum 7.4% is chance. Background fire is itself strongly seasonal (summer farm burning), so the 117× best/worst ratio and 'the gradient' partly measure the season of background fire, not sensor sensitivity to war events. The H1 verdict stands as pre-registered, but the interpretation in §4.1 ignores the paper's own placebo. Also, 'clear night skies' really means 'at least one clear night overpass in the 48-h window', and 'effectively off' describes the worst stratum, not winter as a whole (Nov–Feb recall 0.52%).
raw.evidence: §4.8 line 128 'Recall clearly beats chance only with 3+ clear overpasses or in the H1 best stratum, at about 1.4–1.5× chance'; h1_recall_meta.json ratio 117, ratio_ci_hi null; DEVIATIONS 2026-10-22 night definition; h8_summary.json winter_Nov_Feb recall 0.0052
raw.fix: Abstract: "A FIRMS fire fell within 1 km and 48 hours of 5.0% of held-out confirmed events (7.4% when the window had a clear night overpass in summer; 0.06% in the cloudy, snowy winter stratum). An exploratory same-place placebo matches 3.8%, so most of these matches are background fire." §4.1: add "Part of this gradient is the season of background fire, which the placebo shows is large (§4.8)."

raw.paper_says: **21.8%** of the 29,911 km² Russia gained in C1 front cells fell in the bottom quartile
raw.problem: A conflict expert will read '29,911 km² Russia gained' between April 2022 and July 2024 as a net territorial figure, and it is far too big for that: Russia lost ground over C1 because of the 2022 Kharkiv and Kherson counteroffensives. The number is a gross sum of positive cell-week net flips. Reverse flips in the same cells total about 35,200 km², which also points to VIINA status flicker. The limitations section does not mention flicker.
raw.evidence: data/derived/results/h4_by_opportunity_quartile.csv ru_gain_km2 sum 29,911, ru_loss_km2 sum 35,245; h4_blindspot.json total_ru_gain_km2_c1_front15 29911
raw.fix: "21.8% of the 29,911 km² of gross Ukrainian-to-Russian flips in C1 front cells (the sum of positive weekly cell changes; flips the other way total 35,245 km², so this is not net territorial change) fell in ..."; add to Limitations: "VIINA majority-vote status flickers at the line, inflating gross flips in both directions."

raw.paper_says: We read "Karabakh lower" as a comparison under one common detection rule, the only like-for-like reading, and on that reading it holds
raw.problem: This reading was set when the scoring was written, and the DEVIATIONS entry that records it already states the result ('true at both 1 km and 5 km'). DEVIATIONS says only the event-set and precision choices were fixed before the first run, and the reading is not one of them. Under each case's pre-registered primary rule, Karabakh is higher (12.5% vs 2.9%). The scorecard's 'yes' therefore rests on an interpretation chosen with the answer in view.
raw.evidence: DEVIATIONS 2026-10-27 '"Karabakh lower" ... is read as lower than Sudan under the same detection rule (true at both 1 km and 5 km). The cross-rule primary comparison ... goes the other way.'; verdicts.json H7 'cross-rule primary comparison: False'
raw.fix: Scorecard: "band yes; 'Sudan high' no; 'Karabakh lower' no under the primary rules, yes under a same-rule reading adopted at scoring time". In §4.7 add: "this reading was adopted when the scoring was written, not in PREREG."

raw.paper_says: S-NPP is expected to stop in early November 2026.
raw.problem: This is out of date and has no citation. The project's own planning cites a NASA Earthdata alert that Suomi NPP science-data delivery was to cease on 2 November 2026, and the paper is dated after that (the hand-check material is from 9 Nov). A remote-sensing reader will expect the date, the source, and the distinction between data delivery ending and the satellite itself.
raw.evidence: planning/plan_draft_novelty.md line 19 'NOAA/NESDIS will cease Suomi NPP science-data delivery at 13:00 UTC on 2 November 2026 [NASA Earthdata alert, updated 5 Oct 2026]'
raw.fix: "Suomi NPP science-data delivery was scheduled to cease on 2 November 2026 (NASA Earthdata alert, updated 5 Oct 2026); FIRMS VIIRS now rests on NOAA-20 and NOAA-21." (confirm the cessation happened before submission)

raw.paper_says: Two near-identical sensors looking at the same ground within an hour, with a clear sky, agree only about half the time. Single detections are noisy.
raw.problem: A VIIRS specialist will object to calling this noise. S-NPP and NOAA-20 fly about 50 minutes apart in the same orbit, so small, short-lived fires change or go out between the passes. The two passes also see a given cell at different scan angles, so pixel area (up to about 4× at swath edge, as §4.2 notes) and the detection floor differ between them. Much of the 46% disagreement is expected physics and geometry, not random error, and the test does not separate the two.
raw.evidence: data/derived/results/h3_summary.json definitions: pair = NOAA-20 granule 30–70 min away, no scan-angle matching; §4.2 'edge pixels are about 4.2× the area of nadir pixels'
raw.fix: "Two similar sensors about 50 minutes apart under clear sky agree on about half of fires. Fire change between passes and different viewing geometry account for part of this, so a single detection, and especially a single zero, is weak evidence on its own."

raw.paper_says: Hot summer ground hides small fires by day. So the summer-day fire record is a record of big fires only.
raw.problem: Two remote-sensing issues. First, the fire filter (confidence nominal or high) treats day and night differently: in the VIIRS 375 m product the low-confidence class is mainly daytime pixels with sun glint or a weak (<15 K) I4 anomaly, so dropping it raises the daytime FRP floor by construction. Second, the 5th percentile of detected FRP mixes the detection floor with which fires happen (summer stubble burning is large). A summer-day 5th percentile of 2.22 MW also does not mean 'big fires only'. The verdict stands as pre-registered, but the mechanism and the 'only' are overclaimed.
raw.evidence: PREREG §3 'Fire: ... confidence nominal or high'; verdicts.json H14 summer-day p5 2.22 MW vs winter-night 0.58 MW
raw.fix: "By day the detection floor is higher (solar contamination of the 3.7 µm channel and warmer background; our exclusion of low-confidence pixels, a mainly daytime class, adds to this), and summer fire types differ too. The summer-day record therefore under-represents small fires."

raw.paper_says: **Draft v1, 2026-10-27.** ... ### 5.6 Kyiv strikes (H12, confirmatory, open question)
raw.problem: These are small but visible to a referee. (a) The draft is dated 2026-10-27 but contains 2026-11-09 material (§4.8, DEVIATIONS 2026-11-09). (b) H12 measures FIRMS detections of any type inside Kyiv city, which can include static industrial heat sources, yet the heading and text call them 'strikes'. The national SESOI scaling (× 114 median front cells = 194 km²) and the Newey–West inference are not in PREREG or DEVIATIONS. (c) §3 says C1 was untouched, but PREREG §2 discloses an Economist snapshot with C1-dated files on disk before the tag; the paper does not mention it. (d) 'Nobody had measured how often it misses' is stronger than the prior-art scan supports ('no published omission-rate study turned up').
raw.evidence: DEVIATIONS 2026-11-09 entry; PREREG §3 'Kyiv fires: detections inside Kyiv city ... any type' (§3 Fire 'any type'); verdicts.json H12 criterion '±194 km² (1.70 × 114 median front cells/week)', 'Newey–West(4)'; PREREG §2 Disclosure; planning/scout_prior_art.md line 109
raw.fix: Redate the header to 2026-11-09; retitle §5.6 'Kyiv fires (H12 ...)' and note that the type is not filtered; log the 194 km² scaling and Newey–West as operational choices in DEVIATIONS; add to §3: 'A snapshot of The Economist war-fire files covering C1 dates was on disk before the tag and was not opened (PREREG §2)'; change 'Nobody had measured' to 'We found no published measurement of'.
